subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should OpenClaw change the default source-channel delivery policy so direct and autonomous channel turns suppress intermediate assistant text unless it is final or sent through the message tool?
rationale: The source-level fix boundary is clear, but the default behavior is compatibility-sensitive for users who rely on automatic bare-text replies in direct chats and existing channel workflows.

options.title: Choose a compatible final-only policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and land a policy that suppresses intermediate/private text while preserving explicit message-tool sends and intentional final replies, with upgrade-safe tests.

options.title: Ship an opt-in safety mode first
options.body: Provide a documented opt-in or migration path for customer-facing channels, accepting that the unsafe default remains until a later compatibility decision.

options.title: Keep automatic replies as the contract
options.body: Close or narrow the issue around only specific leak signatures, accepting that ordinary inter-tool prose can still be visible in automatic channel sessions.

recommendation.title: Choose a compatible final-only policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and land a policy that suppresses intermediate/private text while preserving explicit message-tool sends and intentional final replies, with upgrade-safe tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant current source-reply policy and embedded delivery path trace through recent history attributed to Vincent Koc, and the remaining blocker is a cross-channel default-policy choice.
